yarrow.title: Yarrow
yarrow.look: Feathery, finely divided leaves in a fern-like pattern; flat clusters of small white flowers. Crushed leaves smell sharp.

plantain.title: Plantain
plantain.look: Rosette of ribbed leaves with parallel veins and a stringy core when torn; a narrow seed spike.

willow.title: Willow
willow.look: Narrow leaves, often pale underneath; slim flexible twigs; usually near water.

wild_carrot.title: Wild carrot (Queen Anne's lace)
wild_carrot.look: Hairy stem, finely cut leaves, flat white umbrella with one dark floret in the centre, smells of carrot.
wild_carrot.caution: Poison hemlock has a smooth stem with purple blotches. Do not rely on a photo.

poison_hemlock.title: Poison hemlock
poison_hemlock.look: Smooth hairless stem with purple blotches, finely cut leaves, white umbrella flowers. Smells musty.

water_hemlock.title: Water hemlock
water_hemlock.look: Wet ground; clustered tuberous roots; leaves with sharp toothed leaflets and side veins that run to the notches.
water_hemlock.caution: One of the most toxic plants in North America. Every part is deadly.

wild_onion.title: Wild onion
wild_onion.look: Round or flat grass-like leaves that smell of onion when crushed; a bulb at the base.
wild_onion.caution: If it has no onion smell it is not a wild onion. Death camas has no onion smell.

death_camas.title: Death camas
death_camas.look: Onion-like grass leaves from a bulb, cream or greenish flower cluster. No onion smell.

ramps.title: Ramps (wild leek)
ramps.look: Two or three broad smooth leaves per plant in spring, red-purple stalk base, strong onion and garlic smell.
ramps.caution: Check smell on every leaf. False hellebore and lily of the valley grow in the same woods and are deadly.

false_hellebore.title: False hellebore (Indian poke)
false_hellebore.look: Big pleated leaves that wrap the stem in a spiral; wet woods and meadows. No onion smell.

lily_of_valley.title: Lily of the valley
lily_of_valley.look: Two smooth upright leaves, small white bells on an arching stem, red berries.
lily_of_valley.caution: Mistaken for ramps. Every part is deadly.

dandelion.title: Dandelion
dandelion.look: Rosette of toothed leaves, one yellow flower per hollow stalk, milky sap.

chicory.title: Chicory
chicory.look: Sky blue flowers on stiff, nearly leafless stems along roadsides; milky sap.

red_clover.title: Red clover
red_clover.look: Pink-purple round flower heads; three leaflets with a pale V mark.

white_clover.title: White clover
white_clover.look: Low creeping plant, white round flower heads, three leaflets often with a pale band.

burdock.title: Burdock
burdock.look: Very large heart-shaped leaves, hooked burr heads, purple thistle-like flowers.
burdock.caution: Young leaves can be mistaken for foxglove, which is deadly.

foxglove.title: Foxglove
foxglove.look: Fuzzy leaves in a rosette, tall spike of tubular pink-purple bells.
foxglove.caution: Deadly to the heart. Often confused with comfrey in the first year.

comfrey.title: Comfrey
comfrey.look: Rough hairy leaves, bell flowers in curled clusters.
comfrey.caution: Contains liver-damaging compounds. Do not eat or brew it.

cattail.title: Cattail
cattail.look: Tall blade leaves, brown sausage-shaped seed head; wet places.
cattail.caution: Iris leaves look alike before flowering and are toxic.

iris_flag.title: Wild iris (blue flag, yellow flag)
iris_flag.look: Flat sword-shaped leaves in a fan; blue-violet or yellow flowers; wet ground.
iris_flag.caution: Toxic if eaten. Often mistaken for cattail shoots.

wild_strawberry.title: Wild strawberry
wild_strawberry.look: Three toothed leaflets, white five-petal flowers, tiny red berries with seeds on the outside.

brambles.title: Blackberry and raspberry (Rubus)
brambles.look: Arching prickly canes, toothed compound leaves, clustered berries made of tiny beads.

blueberry.title: Blueberry
blueberry.look: Low shrub, small oval leaves, blue berries with a five-point crown at the tip.

cranberry.title: Cranberry
cranberry.look: Trailing evergreen vine in bogs, tiny leaves, red berries.

elderberry.title: Elderberry
elderberry.look: Opposite compound leaves, flat clusters of white flowers, dark purple (or red) berries, pithy stems.
elderberry.caution: Raw berries, leaves and stems are toxic. Cook the berries.

pokeweed.title: Pokeweed
pokeweed.look: Purple-red stems, large leaves, drooping clusters of dark purple berries.
pokeweed.caution: Berries, roots and mature leaves are toxic.

staghorn_sumac.title: Staghorn sumac
staghorn_sumac.look: Fuzzy velvet twigs, long compound leaves, upright red fuzzy berry cones.
staghorn_sumac.caution: Poison sumac has white drooping berries and grows in wet ground.

poison_sumac.title: Poison sumac
poison_sumac.look: Wet ground, smooth stems, leaves with a red stalk, drooping white-grey berries.
poison_sumac.caution: Skin contact causes a severe rash.

poison_ivy.title: Poison ivy
poison_ivy.look: Three leaflets, the middle one on a longer stalk; hairy vine on trees; leaves red in autumn.
poison_ivy.caution: Leaves of three. Skin contact causes a rash. Smoke from burning it is dangerous.

virginia_creeper.title: Virginia creeper
virginia_creeper.look: Five leaflets spread like a hand; climbing vine with tendrils.
virginia_creeper.caution: Berries are toxic. Sometimes mistaken for poison ivy.

stinging_nettle.title: Stinging nettle
stinging_nettle.look: Opposite toothed leaves with stinging hairs, square stem, small green flower strings.
stinging_nettle.caution: Stings on touch. Cooking removes the sting.

lambsquarters.title: Lambsquarters
lambsquarters.look: Diamond-shaped leaves with a white mealy powder underneath.

wood_sorrel.title: Wood sorrel
wood_sorrel.look: Heart-shaped leaflets in threes like a clover, small yellow or pink five-petal flowers; sour taste.

jewelweed.title: Jewelweed
jewelweed.look: Orange or yellow spotted trumpet flowers, pale watery stems, leaves bead up water; seed pods burst when touched.

ostrich_fern.title: Ostrich fern (fiddleheads)
ostrich_fern.look: Tightly coiled fiddlehead with a smooth U-shaped groove on the inside of the stem, papery brown scales.
ostrich_fern.caution: Fiddleheads must be cooked. Bracken is not safe to eat.

bracken.title: Bracken fern
bracken.look: Large triangular fronds on a single stalk, fuzzy coiled shoots, open ground.
bracken.caution: Toxic and linked to cancer. Do not eat.

common_milkweed.title: Common milkweed
common_milkweed.look: Thick stem with milky white sap, big opposite oval leaves, pink ball flower clusters, warty pods.
common_milkweed.caution: Toxic raw. Only a trained forager should use it, and not by photo.

dogbane.title: Dogbane
dogbane.look: Red-tinged stems with milky sap, pointed opposite leaves, tiny white bells, slim paired pods.
dogbane.caution: Toxic to the heart. Looks like milkweed.

mullein.title: Mullein
mullein.look: Large grey fuzzy leaves in a rosette and a tall yellow flower spike in the second year.

st_johns_wort.title: St. John's wort
st_johns_wort.look: Opposite small leaves with see-through dots when held to light; yellow five-petal flowers that stain purple.
st_johns_wort.caution: Interacts with many medicines and causes sun sensitivity.

self_heal.title: Self-heal
self_heal.look: Low plant, square stem, spiky purple flower head with ruffled lips.

goldenrod.title: Goldenrod
goldenrod.look: Tall plume of tiny yellow flowers in late summer, alternate narrow leaves.

white_snakeroot.title: White snakeroot
white_snakeroot.look: Opposite toothed leaves on a branching stem, fuzzy white flower clusters in autumn.
white_snakeroot.caution: Poisons livestock and milk. Do not eat.

jerusalem_artichoke.title: Jerusalem artichoke
jerusalem_artichoke.look: Tall rough sunflower-like plant with small yellow flowers and knobby tubers.

evening_primrose.title: Evening primrose
evening_primrose.look: Tall plant with four-petal yellow flowers that open at dusk, reddish stem.

pineapple_weed.title: Pineapple weed
pineapple_weed.look: Low plant with feathery leaves, yellow-green cone flowers with no petals; smells like pineapple when crushed.

wild_bergamot.title: Wild bergamot
wild_bergamot.look: Square stem, lavender shaggy flower heads, minty oregano smell.

mayapple.title: Mayapple
mayapple.look: Umbrella-like lobed leaves, a single white flower under the leaves, one green-yellow fruit.
mayapple.caution: Everything except the ripe fruit is toxic.

bloodroot.title: Bloodroot
bloodroot.look: One clasped rounded lobed leaf and a white eight-petal flower in early spring; red-orange sap.

baneberry.title: Baneberry
baneberry.look: Compound toothed leaves, a white or red berry cluster on thick red stalks (doll's eyes).

jimsonweed.title: Jimsonweed
jimsonweed.look: Large white trumpet flowers, spiny egg-shaped seed pods, strong smell.

bittersweet_nightshade.title: Bittersweet nightshade
bittersweet_nightshade.look: Climbing vine, purple flowers with a yellow cone, red egg-shaped berries.

monkshood.title: Monkshood
monkshood.look: Deeply cut leaves and tall spikes of hooded blue-purple flowers.
monkshood.caution: Deadly. Even skin contact can numb or harm.

giant_hogweed.title: Giant hogweed
giant_hogweed.look: Huge: stem 5-10 cm wide with purple blotches and stiff hairs, umbrella flower head up to 1 m.
giant_hogweed.caution: Sap plus sunlight causes severe burns. Do not touch.

cow_parsnip.title: Cow parsnip
cow_parsnip.look: Big maple-like leaves, white flat umbrella, hairy hollow stem.
cow_parsnip.caution: Sap can cause burns on sunny skin.

wild_parsnip.title: Wild parsnip
wild_parsnip.look: Yellow umbrella flowers, grooved hollow stem, toothed leaflets.
wild_parsnip.caution: Sap plus sunlight causes burns and blisters.

skunk_cabbage.title: Skunk cabbage
skunk_cabbage.look: Wet ground; mottled purple-maroon hooded flower in late winter; big cabbage-like leaves with a skunky smell.

japanese_knotweed.title: Japanese knotweed
japanese_knotweed.look: Hollow bamboo-like reddish canes, heart-shaped leaves, dense stands.

curly_dock.title: Curly dock
curly_dock.look: Long leaves with wavy ruffled edges, tall rust-red seed stalk.

wintergreen.title: Wintergreen
wintergreen.look: Low evergreen with glossy leaves that smell of wintergreen when crushed; red berries.

wild_rose.title: Wild rose
wild_rose.look: Prickly canes, five-petal pink flowers, red rose hips.
wild_rose.caution: Hips have irritating hairs inside. Remove them.

hawthorn.title: Hawthorn
hawthorn.look: Thorny small tree or shrub with lobed leaves and red apple-like haws.

mountain_laurel.title: Mountain laurel
mountain_laurel.look: Evergreen glossy leaves, clusters of pink-white cup flowers.
mountain_laurel.caution: Leaves, flowers and honey from it are toxic.

sphagnum.title: Sphagnum moss
sphagnum.look: Pale green to red spongy moss in bogs that holds a lot of water.
sphagnum.caution: Wild moss can carry germs. Do not put it on an open wound.

usnea.title: Old man's beard (Usnea)
usnea.look: Pale green hair-like lichen on branches; pull it and the core is a white elastic thread.

cleavers.title: Cleavers
cleavers.look: Sprawling square stem with whorls of narrow leaves that cling by tiny hooks.

moonseed.title: Canada moonseed
moonseed.look: Climbing vine with big lobed leaves, dark blue-black berries each with a single crescent seed.
moonseed.caution: Looks like wild grape. Grapes have several seeds and tendrils. Moonseed has neither.

wild_grape.title: Wild grape
wild_grape.look: Climbing vine with tendrils, toothed lobed leaves, round berries in a bunch.

thistle.title: Thistle
thistle.look: Spiny leaves and stem, round purple flower heads.

spurge.title: Spotted spurge (Euphorbia)
spurge.look: Flat mat of small oval leaves with a dark spot, milky sap.

purslane.title: Purslane
purslane.look: Flat mat of thick succulent paddle leaves with reddish stems; clear sap.
purslane.caution: Spurge has milky sap. Check the sap.

chickweed.title: Chickweed
chickweed.look: Low plant with small oval leaves and one line of hairs along the stem; tiny white deep-notched petals.

common_mallow.title: Common mallow
common_mallow.look: Round lobed leaves on long stalks, small pale pink flowers, round cheese-wheel fruits.

garlic_mustard.title: Garlic mustard
garlic_mustard.look: Heart-shaped toothed leaves smelling of garlic, small white four-petal flowers.

common_juniper.title: Common juniper
common_juniper.look: Low spreading evergreen shrub with sharp needles in threes and blue berry-like cones.
common_juniper.caution: Do not mix it up with yew, which is deadly.

yew.title: Yew (Canada yew)
yew.look: Flat dark green needles with two pale lines underneath, red fleshy cup berries; low shrub.
yew.caution: Needles, seeds and bark are deadly.

balsam_fir.title: Balsam fir
balsam_fir.look: Flat blunt needles with two white lines underneath, upright cones, smooth bark with resin blisters, spicy smell.

red_spruce.title: Red spruce
red_spruce.look: Square four-sided stiff needles that roll between your fingers, hanging cones, reddish scaly bark.

white_spruce.title: White spruce
white_spruce.look: Four-sided blue-green needles, slim hanging cones; needles smell strongly when crushed.

black_spruce.title: Black spruce
black_spruce.look: Bog tree with a thin top, short needles, small round cones that stay on the tree.

white_pine.title: Eastern white pine
white_pine.look: Soft needles in bundles of five, long slim cones, tiered branches.

red_pine.title: Red pine
red_pine.look: Long needles in bundles of two that snap cleanly, orange-red flaky bark.

eastern_hemlock.title: Eastern hemlock (the tree)
eastern_hemlock.look: Flat short needles with two white lines underneath on tiny stalks, tiny cones, drooping top.
eastern_hemlock.caution: The tree is not the poison hemlock plants. Poison and water hemlock are herbs with umbrella flowers.

eastern_red_cedar.title: Eastern red cedar
eastern_red_cedar.look: Scaly green leaves or sharp awls, blue berry-like cones, shredding reddish bark.

northern_white_cedar.title: Northern white cedar
northern_white_cedar.look: Flat fans of scale-like leaves, small cones, stringy bark; wet ground.

tamarack.title: Tamarack (larch)
tamarack.look: Soft needles in tufts that turn gold and drop in autumn.

sugar_maple.title: Sugar maple
sugar_maple.look: Five-lobed leaf with smooth rounded gaps, opposite branches, grey furrowed bark.

red_maple.title: Red maple
red_maple.look: Three- to five-lobed leaf with toothed edges and sharp gaps, red twigs and buds.

paper_birch.title: Paper birch
paper_birch.look: White bark peeling in papery sheets with dark marks; toothed oval leaves.

yellow_birch.title: Yellow birch
yellow_birch.look: Silver-yellow bark that peels in curly strips; twigs smell of wintergreen when scratched.

american_beech.title: American beech
american_beech.look: Smooth blue-grey bark, toothed oval leaves with straight veins, pale leaves that stay in winter.

white_oak.title: White oak
white_oak.look: Rounded leaf lobes, pale scaly bark.

red_oak.title: Red oak
red_oak.look: Pointed leaf lobes with bristle tips, ridged bark with pale stripes.

american_elm.title: American elm
american_elm.look: Leaves with uneven bases and double teeth, vase shape.

quaking_aspen.title: Quaking aspen
quaking_aspen.look: Round leaves on flat stalks that tremble, smooth pale green-white bark.

black_cherry.title: Black cherry
black_cherry.look: Dark scaly bark like burnt potato chips, glossy toothed leaves, dark berries.
black_cherry.caution: Leaves, pits and bark contain cyanide compounds. Wilted leaves are dangerous.

shagbark_hickory.title: Shagbark hickory
shagbark_hickory.look: Long loose plates of bark curling at the ends; compound leaves; hard nuts in husks.

basswood.title: Basswood (linden)
basswood.look: Large heart-shaped lopsided leaves, nut-like balls hanging from a leafy strip.

black_walnut.title: Black walnut
black_walnut.look: Compound leaves of many leaflets, dark ridged bark, round green husked nuts.

sassafras.title: Sassafras
sassafras.look: Leaves of three shapes on one tree (oval, mitten, three-lobed); spicy smell when crushed.

sycamore.title: American sycamore
sycamore.look: Bark flaking off in patches of white and brown, big lobed leaves, ball fruits.

witch_hazel.title: Witch hazel
witch_hazel.look: Wavy-edged uneven leaves, yellow ribbon flowers in late autumn.

fly_agaric.title: Fly agaric
fly_agaric.look: Red or orange cap with white warts, white gills, a ring on the stem and a bulb at the base.
fly_agaric.caution: Toxic. Related to the deadly Amanitas.

death_cap.title: Death cap
death_cap.look: Olive-green to pale cap, white gills, a skirt-like ring and a cup (volva) at the base.
death_cap.caution: One cap can kill. Symptoms start many hours later, after which it is already working on the liver.

destroying_angel.title: Destroying angel
destroying_angel.look: Pure white cap, gills, ring and stem, with a cup at the base that may be buried.
destroying_angel.caution: Deadly. Looks like button mushrooms and young puffballs.

deadly_galerina.title: Deadly galerina
deadly_galerina.look: Small brown mushroom on rotting wood with a thin ring and rusty brown spores.
deadly_galerina.caution: Deadly. Grows on the same logs as honey mushrooms.

webcaps.title: Webcaps (Cortinarius)
webcaps.look: Rusty-brown spores, a web-like veil on young caps, often on the ground in woods.
webcaps.caution: Some are deadly to the kidneys. Never eat a brown mushroom you cannot identify.

chanterelle.title: Chanterelle
chanterelle.look: Golden or orange funnel with blunt forked ridges that run down the stem, not true gills; fruity smell.
chanterelle.caution: Jack-o'-lantern has true gills, grows in clusters on wood and is toxic.

jack_o_lantern.title: Jack-o'-lantern
jack_o_lantern.look: Orange clusters on wood or buried roots with true gills that run down the stem; glows faintly in the dark.

chicken_of_the_woods.title: Chicken of the woods
chicken_of_the_woods.look: Bright orange and yellow shelves with no gills on trees, soft when young.
chicken_of_the_woods.caution: Some people react badly, and growths on conifers or eucalyptus can be harmful.

hen_of_the_woods.title: Hen of the woods (maitake)
hen_of_the_woods.look: Big clump of grey-brown overlapping fronds at the base of oaks; pores instead of gills.

morel.title: True morel
morel.look: Hollow throughout when cut lengthwise, cap fused to the stem, honeycomb pits.
morel.caution: False morels are deadly. Cut every one open.

false_morel.title: False morel
false_morel.look: Wrinkled brain-like cap that is not hollow-honeycombed; stem cottony inside.

giant_puffball.title: Puffball
giant_puffball.look: Round white ball with no stem or gills; solid white inside when cut.
giant_puffball.caution: A young Amanita looks like a puffball. Cut it open: any outline of a cap and stem means leave it.

lions_mane.title: Lion's mane
lions_mane.look: White hanging icicle-like spines on trees.

oyster_mushroom.title: Oyster mushroom
oyster_mushroom.look: Shelf-shaped grey-tan caps with gills running down to a short side stem, on wood.
oyster_mushroom.caution: Do not confuse it with other shelf fungi that have gills.

turkey_tail.title: Turkey tail
turkey_tail.look: Thin tough shelves with colored concentric bands and a white pore underside.

birch_polypore.title: Birch polypore (razor strop)
birch_polypore.look: Rounded grey-white shelf on dead birch; the pore side is white; used as a strop.
birch_polypore.caution: Survival history only. Do not eat it.

reishi.title: Reishi (hemlock varnish shelf)
reishi.look: Glossy varnished red-brown shelf on a stalk or the side of a tree.

honey_mushroom.title: Honey mushroom
honey_mushroom.look: Clusters of honey-coloured caps on wood with a ring; white spores.
honey_mushroom.caution: The deadly galerina looks like it.

shaggy_mane.title: Shaggy mane
shaggy_mane.look: Tall white cylinder cap with shaggy scales that melts into ink.

bolete.title: Bolete
bolete.look: Fat stem with a sponge of pores instead of gills under the cap.
bolete.caution: Red-pored and bitter ones are toxic. Do not eat on a photo.

green_spored_parasol.title: Green-spored parasol
green_spored_parasol.look: Big scaly cap with a ring; gills turn green with age; lawns.
green_spored_parasol.caution: The most common mushroom poisoning in North America.

hedgehog_mushroom.title: Hedgehog mushroom
hedgehog_mushroom.look: Pale orange cap with soft spines instead of gills.

tinder_fungus.title: Tinder fungus
tinder_fungus.look: Hoof-shaped grey woody shelf on birch and beech; used for tinder.

chaga.title: Chaga
chaga.look: Black charcoal-like crust on birch with an orange inside.

white_tailed_deer.title: White-tailed deer
white_tailed_deer.look: Brown coat, white underside, tail raised like a white flag.

moose.title: Moose
moose.look: Huge with a long face, dewlap, and broad flat antlers on bulls.
moose.caution: Do not approach. Cows with calves and bulls in rut charge.

elk.title: Elk
elk.look: Large with a pale rump and branching antlers.

black_bear.title: Black bear
black_bear.look: Black or brown with a straight muzzle and no shoulder hump.
black_bear.caution: Keep distance, never run, store food away from camp.

coyote.title: Coyote
coyote.look: Slim dog-like with a bushy low tail and pointed ears.

red_fox.title: Red fox
red_fox.look: Red coat, black legs, white tail tip.

bobcat.title: Bobcat
bobcat.look: Short tail with a black tip, tufted ears, spotted coat.

porcupine.title: Porcupine
porcupine.caution: Quills cannot be thrown. Keep dogs away.

striped_skunk.title: Striped skunk
striped_skunk.look: Black with white stripes down the back.

beaver.title: Beaver
beaver.look: Flat paddle tail, dam and cut sapling stumps.

snowshoe_hare.title: Snowshoe hare
snowshoe_hare.look: Large back feet, coat white in winter and brown in summer.

wild_turkey.title: Wild turkey
wild_turkey.look: Large dark bird with a bare head and fanned tail.

ruffed_grouse.title: Ruffed grouse
ruffed_grouse.look: Brown barred bird with a fan tail and dark neck ruff.

bald_eagle.title: Bald eagle
bald_eagle.look: Large dark bird with a white head and tail on adults.

great_horned_owl.title: Great horned owl
great_horned_owl.look: Large owl with ear tufts and yellow eyes.

canada_goose.title: Canada goose
canada_goose.look: Black neck and head with a white chin strap.

rattlesnake.title: Rattlesnake
rattlesnake.look: Thick body, triangular head, a rattle on the tail.
rattlesnake.caution: Venomous. Back away slowly. Call emergency services after a bite.

copperhead.title: Copperhead
copperhead.look: Copper head, tan body with hourglass bands.
copperhead.caution: Venomous. Back away slowly. Call emergency services after a bite.

cottonmouth.title: Cottonmouth
cottonmouth.look: Heavy dark water snake with a white mouth when it gapes.
cottonmouth.caution: Venomous. Back away slowly. Call emergency services after a bite.

eastern_garter_snake.title: Garter snake
eastern_garter_snake.look: Slim, three pale stripes along the body.

northern_water_snake.title: Northern water snake
northern_water_snake.caution: Not venomous but it bites hard. Often mistaken for a copperhead.

blacklegged_tick.title: Blacklegged (deer) tick
blacklegged_tick.look: Tiny dark tick; adult females have an orange-red body and black plate.
blacklegged_tick.caution: Carries Lyme and other diseases. Remove with tweezers close to the skin and keep the date.

american_dog_tick.title: American dog tick
american_dog_tick.look: Larger brown tick with white-cream markings on the back.
american_dog_tick.caution: Can carry spotted fever. Remove with tweezers close to the skin.

lone_star_tick.title: Lone star tick
lone_star_tick.look: Reddish-brown tick with one white dot on the back of females.
lone_star_tick.caution: Bites can cause meat allergy. Remove with tweezers close to the skin.

black_widow.title: Black widow
black_widow.look: Shiny black spider with a red hourglass underneath.
black_widow.caution: Venomous. Seek care after a bite.

bald_faced_hornet.title: Bald-faced hornet
bald_faced_hornet.look: Black and white wasp with a grey paper nest the size of a football.
bald_faced_hornet.caution: Stings hurt and are dangerous if allergic.

yellowjacket.title: Yellowjacket
yellowjacket.look: Black and yellow wasp that nests underground.
yellowjacket.caution: Stings hurt and are dangerous if allergic.

wild_boar.title: Wild boar (feral hog)
wild_boar.look: Dark bristly pig with a long snout.
wild_boar.caution: Can be aggressive. Cook the meat fully.

deer_track.title: Deer track
deer_track.look: Two teardrop toes forming a heart shape, pointed forward, sometimes with two small dewclaw dots.

bear_track.title: Bear track
bear_track.look: Wide five-toed print with claw dots and a broad heel pad.

canine_track.title: Coyote, fox or dog track
canine_track.look: Four toes with claw marks and an X shape between the toes and the pad.

raccoon_track.title: Raccoon track
raccoon_track.look: Five long finger-like toes like a tiny human hand.

moose_track.title: Moose track
moose_track.look: Large pointed split hoof print, over 10 cm long.

turkey_track.title: Turkey track
turkey_track.look: Three forward toes and a short back toe, in a long stride.

bobcat_track.title: Bobcat track
bobcat_track.look: Four toes with no claw marks and a three-lobed heel pad.

rabbit_track.title: Rabbit or hare track
rabbit_track.look: Two large hind feet side by side ahead of two smaller front prints.

deer_scat.title: Deer scat
deer_scat.look: Small dark oval pellets in a pile.

bear_scat.title: Bear scat
bear_scat.look: Large tubular scat with berries, seeds or hair in it.
bear_scat.caution: Fresh bear sign means a bear is near. Be bear aware.

coyote_scat.title: Coyote or fox scat
coyote_scat.look: Twisted tubular scat with hair and bone and a tapered end.

moose_scat.title: Moose scat
moose_scat.look: Large oval wood-fibre pellets, or a clump in summer.

raccoon_scat.title: Raccoon scat
raccoon_scat.look: Blunt-ended tubes with berry seeds and bits of shell, often at a latrine.
raccoon_scat.caution: Raccoon latrines can carry roundworm. Do not touch them.

rabbit_scat.title: Rabbit scat
rabbit_scat.look: Round pea-sized pellets that are flat on the sides.
